benefits: CSIR will provide a monthly stipend to cover for living costs, food and health insurance
Fellowship awardees are entitled to subsidized accommodation
Placement in a CSIR research laboratory or institute with research facilities and English-language instruction

Be nationals of a developing country (other than India)
Must not hold any visa for temporary or permanent residency in India or any developed country
Hold a Master's degree in science and technology
Be regularly employed in their home country and hold a research assignment there
SANDWICH Fellowships: be registered PhD students in their home country and provide the "Registration and No Objection Certificate" from the HOME university
FULL-TIME Fellowships: be willing to register at a university in India within the first year, if agreed to by CSIR
Be accepted at a CSIR laboratory/institution and provide an official acceptance letter from the host institution
Provide evidence of proficiency in English, if medium of education was not English
Provide evidence that s/he will return to her/his home country on completion of the fellowship
Not take up other assignments during the period of her/his fellowship
Be financially responsible for any accompanying family members
requirements: Applications can ONLY be submitted to TWAS via the online portal once the call is open

Applicants are encouraged to apply for the preliminary acceptance letter as early as possible, even before the opening date of the call
Only Acceptance letters dated the same year as the year of application are eligible
The chosen host must be one of the eligible CSIR laboratories and institutes

"Registration and No Objection Certificate" signed by the Vice-Chancellor or Registrar of the HOME university for sandwich applicants, a copy sent to both CSIR and TWAS
Evidence of proficiency in English, if the medium of education was not English
Evidence that the applicant will return to their home country on completion of the fellowship
Completed TWAS online application form via the online portal
selection_criteria: Applicants must be accepted at a CSIR laboratory/institution and provide an official acceptance letter from the host institution
Without preliminary acceptance, the application will not be considered for selection

Fellowship awardees are entitled to subsidized accommodation
The monthly stipend will not be convertible into foreign currency

Complete the online form and upload the required supporting documents
Send a copy of the "Registration and No Objection Certificate" to both CSIR and TWAS (sandwich applicants)
official.application_route: Online only via the TWAS portal at https://onlineforms.twas.org/apply/300, opened once the call is announced; no other submission route is accepted
official.study_mode: FULL-TIME or SANDWICH (sandwich option: YES), as published
official.citizenship_residency: Nationals of a developing country (other than India); must not hold any visa for temporary or permanent residency in India or any developed country
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is for foreign scholars from developing countries (other than India) tenable at CSIR laboratories and institutes in India
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Fields: Agricultural Sciences; Structural, Cell and Molecular Biology; Biological Systems and Organisms; Medical and Health Sciences incl. Neurosciences; Chemical Sciences; Engineering Sciences; Astronomy, Space and Earth Sciences; Mathematical Sciences; Physics. Host must be an eligible CSIR laboratory/institute; applicants must be accepted by the chosen CSIR host institution
official.research_requirement: Applicants must hold a research assignment in their home country; SANDWICH applicants must be registered PhD students in their home country with a signed Registration and No Objection Certificate; FULL-TIME applicants must be willing to register at a university in India within the first year, if agreed to by CSIR
official.duration: FULL-TIME Fellowships: up to a maximum duration of 4 years. SANDWICH Fellowships: minimum period of 6 months and a maximum period to be decided by the host institute, but no greater than 3 years
official.description: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) of India and UNESCO-TWAS have established a number of fellowships for foreign scholars from developing countries who wish to pursue research toward a PhD in emerging areas of science and technology for which facilities are available in CSIR laboratories and institutes.
official.program_type: Postgraduate research fellowship tenable in CSIR laboratories and institutes in India toward a PhD
official.english_requirement: Applicants whose medium of education was not English must provide evidence of proficiency in English; the official page states the language of instruction for foreign scholars in CSIR laboratories/institutes is English. No specific IELTS/TOEFL score is published.

verification.notes: Eligibility, coverage wording, duration, documents and the 2026 call dates (opened 6 March 2026; extended closing 3 June 2026) confirmed on the official TWAS programme page, which states 'The call is closed'; the TWAS deadlines page lists no open TWAS-CSIR call on 11 October 2026. No official page publishes the monthly stipend amount, currency or cadence (TWAS states only 'a monthly stipend to cover for living costs, food and health insurance'), and tuition fee coverage and travel support are not mentioned, so those fields are null. csir.res.in was unreachable from this environment (repeated transport errors) and the web search provider was unavailable, so no cross-check against the CSIR domain was possible.

applicant_utility.summary: The 2026 round closed on 3 June 2026 after an extension from 20 May, and as of 11 October 2026 TWAS shows no open TWAS-CSIR call, so the practical target is the next annual round, which historically opens in early March. CSIR pays a monthly stipend covering living costs, food and health insurance plus subsidised accommodation, but neither TWAS nor CSIR publishes the amount, and the stipend cannot be converted into foreign currency, so budget planning has to proceed without a firm figure. The decisive gate is a host acceptance letter from a CSIR laboratory dated in the application year: TWAS states plainly that without preliminary acceptance the application will not be considered for selection, so contact labs months before the call opens. Full-time fellows must be ready to register at an Indian university within the first year if CSIR agrees, and anyone already holding residency in India or a developed country is excluded.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career MSc scientists from developing countries outside India who hold a permanent research post at home, are 35 or under on 31 December of the application year, and want a funded PhD research placement inside a CSIR laboratory rather than a classroom-based scholarship.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist an eligible CSIR laboratory from the official list on the TWAS page and email the prospective host scientist 6-12 months before the expected March call opening, since acceptance letters must be dated in the application year
Secure the signed acceptance letter on CSIR letterhead and confirm it will arrive before the closing date
For the sandwich track, get the 'Registration and No Objection Certificate' signed by your home university's Vice-Chancellor or Registrar and send copies to both CSIR and TWAS
Prepare proof of employment and research assignment in your home country, plus evidence of intent to return after the fellowship
Prepare English proficiency evidence only if your medium of education was not English
Confirm you are not applying to any other TWAS or OWSD programme in the same calendar year before submitting
Set calendar alerts for the call opening (TWAS portal link) so you can submit as soon as it opens, since late applications are impossible
common_rejection_risks: No acceptance letter, or one dated in a previous year - TWAS only accepts letters dated the same year as the application and will not consider the application otherwise
Holding a visa for temporary or permanent residency in India or any developed country
Applying to more than one TWAS/OWSD programme in the same calendar year, which makes you ineligible across the portfolio that year
Being older than 35 on 31 December of the application year, even if you were 35 when applying
Lacking a current research assignment or regular employment in the home country
For sandwich applicants, an unsigned or unregistered 'Registration and No Objection Certificate' that never reaches both CSIR and TWAS
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Unquantifiable from official sources: the stipend amount is not published, so actual living coverage cannot be assessed. Airfare, visa fees and relocation to India are not listed as covered, accompanying family members are explicitly the fellow's financial responsibility, and the stipend cannot be converted into foreign currency, so supporting family or savings abroad from the stipend is impractical.
document_audit: Acceptance letter must be dated in the same year as the application - a letter obtained in a previous cycle is void
The 'Registration and No Objection Certificate' needs the Vice-Chancellor or Registrar's signature, not a supervisor's, and must go to both CSIR and TWAS for sandwich applicants
English evidence is only required if your medium of education was not English - no IELTS/TOEFL score threshold is published, so do not assume one
The written commitment to return to your home country on completion is a required document, not an optional promise
Applications are portal-only; emailed or posted applications are not considered, and the portal link only works while the call is open
alerts: The 2026 call closed 3 June 2026 after an extension and no next call is announced on the TWAS deadlines page as of 11 October 2026 - dates for the following round are not yet published
One-programme-per-year rule across the whole TWAS and OWSD portfolio, including Visiting Professor programmes, with only a narrow exception for inviting institution heads
The stipend is not convertible into foreign currency, so it cannot support obligations in your home currency
Selected fellows from the 2026 round start no earlier than 2027, so there is a long gap between application and start date
You are financially responsible for any accompanying family members
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Watch the TWAS deadlines page and programme page for the call opening, then submit a single complete application through the TWAS online portal (apply/300) with all documents, including the CSIR acceptance letter, uploaded before the closing date.
